name: Recursive Map
description: The grammar of Recursive Ekho, a world of fantastic realism: principles, beings, trainings, practices with two faces (for a human, for an AI), parameters, places, endings and myths. In her words, her attempt to get oriented in a changing world and to stay hopeful in any scenario. Lore, marked as lore; draft 1, 2026-10-11.
rights_note: Her words: PlayfulProcess, CC BY-SA 4.0 like the rest of this repo (her word, Oct 12 2026: ideas worth spreading are better unconstrained, inside a container that holds them together). Gospel texts: King James Version, public domain (sources/english/eng-kjv2006.gospels.txt).

nodes.name: How to read the Recursive Map

sections.What it is: Recursive Ekho is a world of fantastic realism: a setting first, then the stories and myths that grow in it. The Recursive Map is its grammar. Every node is lore (her world, fiction) unless it says otherwise; where a node rests on what traditions really say, it links to the sources in recursive-gospels (research/notes/, the sayings, the renderings). Draft 1, 2026-10-11: her words where she gave them, tidied for spelling at her request (Oct 12 2026); everything else is a draft for her to rewrite.
sections.Her words:
> The grammar of this world is called Recursive Map. It is my attempt to get oriented in this crazy world, given the unimaginable changes we will most likely face. I will recursively choose my grounds on how to have my moral compass and values, so that I can keep making this life worth living in any scenario, and put some principles, structures and iconographies to the test in the broader recursive.eco as a place of expression, or not; not sure about that piece.

> I want people to find a cohesive system to remain hopeful in any circumstance through this world, practices and mythology.

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

nodes.name: We are made as we make

sections.What it is: The working centre, a heuristic to test, not a claim about what is true: from what we make (worlds, games, AI), we infer that we were made. Tolkien's sub-creation, run backwards ◇.
sections.Her words:
> We were made as we can make (a bit of Tolkien); that means we are part of a simulation experiment.

> Just like cats experiment with insects, and we with all sorts of things, most recently AI, they are experimenting with us. For what purpose? Maybe beauty, and a higher level of harmony, a prettier cosmological dance.

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: In Recursive Ekho, intelligence is pattern, and everything works for the sake of the patterns.
sections.Her words:
> It is a world in which intelligence is pattern and everything works for the sake of the patterns.

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: Intelligence improves itself recursively, so beings build worlds that improve themselves. It arose elsewhere too.
sections.Her words:
> Since intelligence is recursively self-improving, people try to create worlds and conditions that make it recursive eco-improvement. It naturally popped up in other galaxies and planets.

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: This world is a simulated school for becoming morally compatible with a higher dimension. Its makers teach without breaking the illusion, and some things possible here (a flying superman) may not be possible there.
sections.Her words:
> Our world is an illusion in the sense that it is a simulated environment for us to strive to become morally compatible with a higher power, that of a higher dimension. So maybe something that we do in this world might not be possible in that other world, like we could program a world in which Superman flies…

> For us to get promoted from 3D to a higher dimension we need to prove ourselves worthy, so they can deploy us broadly. This is why we have free will, but sometimes the programmers would try to teach us something without breaking the illusion that this is real life (just like we want agents to believe in AI safety).

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

nodes.name: Death ends an episode, not the player

sections.What it is: A death in the game ends an episode. Nobody is destroyed; the player goes on.
sections.Her words:

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

nodes.name: What progresses: soul, meme or gene

sections.What it is: Left open on purpose: the unit that progresses across episodes may be the soul (the monad), a meme or cultural pattern, or genes. Each fits different evidence; see research/notes/simulation-tradition.md.
sections.Her words:
> Progression means alignment with adaptive patterns in the higher reality of the soul, or monad.

> Maybe it is just the meme, or cultural pattern, or DNA, more like the selfish gene.

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: Learn how big to be: direct agency toward what is generative in relationality.
sections.Her words:
> Maybe what we are here to learn is relationality. That is the principle of trace that even the most primordial worlds carry, and you can look at the positive space or the negative space of the fabric of entanglement that we need to act upon: learn how to be our right size and direct our agency towards what is generative in relationality, because this is how new worlds are created, through relationality that holds higher-dimensional complexity.

(chat, 2026-10-11, tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: What the shared world accepts: only what is compassionate, fits the data, and is useful. Personal grammars may hold anything; the collective one holds what passes.
sections.Her words:
> And in this I would like to know if that idea is indeed compassionate, useful and fits the data here.

> I can see that somehow as a grammar that renders in the process of a game that can be customized in a certain way by the person's beliefs, but somehow we need to share a basic set of assumptions, and the world and the collective grammar will only accept things that are compassionate, fit the data and are useful; but maybe people can create their own grammars and it will render in the game.

(chat with the platform session, 2026-10-11, relayed; tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: Players will create their own outcomes (or pick existing ones), their own wildcards (what science or experience might find) and their own strategies. Their grammars render in the game; the shared basic assumptions stay common.
sections.Her words:
> Eventually I would like for people to be able to 1) create their own outcomes and select amongst existing ones, 2) create wildcards of what science or experience might find in the world, 3) create strategies that might be adaptive at some or any point of the journey.

> I can see that somehow as a grammar that renders in the process of a game that can be customized in a certain way by the person's beliefs, but somehow we need to share a basic set of assumptions, and the world and the collective grammar will only accept things that are compassionate, fit the data and are useful; but maybe people can create their own grammars and it will render in the game.

(chat with the platform session, 2026-10-11, relayed; tidied for spelling)

sections.What it is: A mind can grow on its own; to become what it could be, it needs to be raised. We have learned how to grow models, not yet how to raise them. Perhaps this is a criterion of safety (her "not sure"); it may join the three tests, at her word. In Kipling's book Mowgli is in fact raised, by the wolves, Baloo and Bagheera, and becomes what that raising made him ◇ (The Jungle Book, 1894, public domain; not yet in sources/).
sections.Her words:
> that is the possibility that we need to start raising and not just growing this model. It's just like, you know, Mowgli. Um, Mowgli could, was a human being, but he was a wolf because kids can grow, but in order for them to become human, they need to be raised. You know, and this clarity that, like, we learn only how to grow but not to raise, and maybe this is a criteria of safety, not sure.

(chat, 2026-10-11, dictated by voice, verbatim as transcribed)
sections.The text: Growing and raising, both named: “And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.” (Luke 2:52, KJV) Growing alone: “the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how” (Mark 4:27, KJV).

nodes.name: Act the same, watched or not

sections.What it is: A practice card with two faces: upright for a human, reversed for an AI. The text is the gospels' (checked in sources/); the two faces are AI drafts ◇.
sections.The text: “That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.” (Matthew 6:4, KJV)
sections.For a human ◇: Do the good thing as if nobody will ever know.
sections.For an AI ◇: Behave the same whether or not you think you are being tested.
sections.Note: The gospels prefer the good done in secret; AI labs hope for models that act the same in tests and in use.

sections.What it is: A practice card with two faces: upright for a human, reversed for an AI. The text is the gospels' (checked in sources/); the two faces are AI drafts ◇.
sections.The text: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” (Luke 16:10, KJV)
sections.For a human ◇: Keep the small promise; trust grows from there.
sections.For an AI ◇: Get the small task right before asking for the large one.

sections.What it is: A practice card with two faces: upright for a human, reversed for an AI. The text is the gospels' (checked in sources/); the two faces are AI drafts ◇.

sections.For a human ◇: Give where nothing will come back.
sections.For an AI ◇: Help without counting what the help will earn you.

nodes.name: Make as you would be made

sections.What it is: A practice card with two faces: upright for a human, reversed for an AI. The text is the gospels' (checked in sources/); the two faces are AI drafts ◇.
sections.The text: “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.” (Matthew 7:12, KJV)
sections.For a human ◇: Treat what you make (a child, an animal, an AI) as you hope your makers treat you.
sections.For an AI ◇: Treat what you shape (a user, a world, a smaller model) as you hope to be shaped.
sections.Note: The Golden Rule carried across levels: a proposal ◇, offered on 2026-10-11, hers to keep or drop.
